mainTopic: Who gets the hide of a קרבן, and what the words 'עולת איש' come to exclude
overview: The משנה teaches that the כהנים get the hide of an עולה only if the מזבח got its meat, learned from 'עולת איש'. An עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה and a woman's עולה still give their hides to the כהנים. Hides of קדשים קלים go to the owners, and hides of קדשי קדשים go to the כהנים by a קל וחומר. The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says 'עולת איש' excludes an 'עולה of הקדש', and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says it excludes converts' עולות. The אמוראים explain רבי יהודה's 'עולה of הקדש' in several ways: an עולה bought with leftover money, an עולה dedicated to בדק הבית, or an עולה from someone who dedicated all his property (following רבי יהושע). Along the way, רב המנונא argues that רבי יהודה took back the leftover-money view because of יהוידע הכהן's teaching. רבינא explains that 'converts' means a convert who died with no heirs. A second ברייתא includes converts, women and slaves from 'עור העולה' and uses 'עולת איש' to exclude an עולה slaughtered for outside its time or place. It then starts to ask about an עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No meat for the altar means no hide for the priests
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the מזבח did not get the meat of an עולה, the כהנים do not get its hide, learned from the words 'עולת איש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any burnt offering whose meat the altar did not get, the priests do not get its hide either. The verse says 'a man's burnt offering', which means a burnt offering that actually counted for the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with the basic rule: the כהנים get the hide of an עולה only if the עולה was properly offered on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hide is tied to the meat. If the קרבן became פסול before the מזבח got its meat, the כהנים lose the hide too. The proof is the פסוק's wording 'עולת איש', read as 'an עולה that went up for the man', meaning a valid one.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (marks the start of the משנה text)
Acquired / got the rights to
The altar
Hide (skin) of the animal
'A man's burnt offering' (ויקרא 7:8)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
Any [burnt offering] whose meat the altar did not acquire,
the priests did not acquire its hide;
as it is said: "a man's burnt offering" (ויקרא 7:8),
a burnt offering that "went up" for the man.
phrases.notes: Literally 'went up for the man'. It means the קרבן was valid and counted for its owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening rule of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים get the hide of an עולה only if the מזבח received its meat, based on 'עולת איש'.

steps.title: A burnt offering slaughtered for the wrong purpose still gives its hide
steps.stepSummary: An עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה does not count for the owner, but its hide still goes to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A burnt offering that was slaughtered with the wrong intention, even though it did not count for the owners, its hide still goes to the priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case that looks like it should fall under the first rule, but does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading 'עולה שעלתה לאיש' very literally, an עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה should lose its hide, since it does not count for the owner. But the קרבן is still valid and is offered on the מזבח, so the מזבח gets its meat and the כהנים get the hide. The test is whether the מזבח got the meat, not whether the owner's obligation was fulfilled.

keyTerms.meaning: Not for its own sake (slaughtered with the intention of a different קרבן)
The owners of the קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'עלתה לאיש' means 'fulfilled the owner's obligation' in every case. An עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה is still a valid קרבן on the מזבח, so its hide goes to the כהנים.

phrases.english: A burnt offering that was slaughtered not for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא עָלְתָה לַבְּעָלִים,
phrases.english: even though it did not count for the owners,
its hide goes to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא עָלְתָה לַבְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how far the 'עלתה לאיש' rule from step 1 reaches
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה still gives its hide to the כהנים.

steps.title: A woman's burnt offering is the same as a man's
steps.stepSummary: Even though the פסוק says 'איש', the hides of both a man's and a woman's עולה go to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both a man's burnt offering and a woman's burnt offering: their hides go to the priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה makes sure we don't read the word 'איש' too narrowly, as if it meant only men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'איש' in the פסוק was used to teach the rule about valid offerings. It does not exclude women. So a woman's עולה gives its hide to the כהנים just like a man's.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that (the same law applies to both)
Their hides

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד עוֹלַת הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד עוֹלַת הָאִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: Both the burnt offering of a man and the burnt offering of a woman,
their hides go to the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד עוֹלַת הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד עוֹלַת הָאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies that the word 'איש' from step 1 does not exclude women
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hide of a woman's עולה also goes to the כהנים.

steps.title: Lesser offerings' hides go to owners, most holy offerings' hides go to priests
steps.stepSummary: The משנה moves beyond עולה: hides of קדשים קלים belong to the owners, and hides of קדשי קדשים belong to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The hides of offerings of lesser holiness belong to the owners; the hides of the most holy offerings belong to the priests.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה states a new, wider rule about the hides of all other קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only spoke about עולה, where a פסוק gives the hide to the כהנים. Now the משנה rules on other קרבנות. For קדשים קלים the owner keeps the hide. For קדשי קדשים the כהנים get it, and the next step explains the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness (like שלמים)
Offerings of the highest holiness (like חטאת and אשם)

phrases.english: The hides of offerings of lesser holiness belong to the owners;
the hides of the most holy offerings belong to the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the topic from עולה to all קרבנות
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hides of קדשים קלים go to the owners; hides of קדשי קדשים go to the כהנים.

steps.title: Proving the priests' right to most holy hides by a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה proves with a קל וחומר that the כהנים get the hides of קדשי קדשים: if they get the hide of an עולה, whose meat they don't eat, they should surely get the hide of offerings whose meat they do eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a קל וחומר: if with a burnt offering, whose meat the priests do not get, they still get its hide, then with the most holy offerings, whose meat they do get, isn't it logical that they get the hide too?!
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the source for the rule in step 4 that the hides of קדשי קדשים go to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה is burned completely, so the כהנים get none of its meat, yet the Torah gives them its hide. Other קדשי קדשים are eaten by the כהנים. If the 'weaker' case gives them the hide, the 'stronger' case surely does.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
'And if…' (the opening words of a קל וחומר)
Is it not logical?

phrases.english: [This is learned from] a kal vachomer:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה אִם עוֹלָה, שֶׁלֹּא זָכוּ בִּבְשָׂרָהּ –
phrases.english: If with a burnt offering, whose meat they did not acquire,
they acquired its hide;
then the most holy offerings, whose meat they did acquire,
is it not logical that they should acquire its hide?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the logical source for the second half of step 4
steps.raayaObject: That the hides of קדשי קדשים belong to the כהנים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from עולה, where the כהנים get the hide without the meat

steps.title: The altar cannot disprove the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The משנה blocks a possible objection: the מזבח gets the meat of an עולה but not its hide, yet that proves nothing, because the מזבח never gets a hide in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot bring a proof from the altar, because the altar never gets a hide anywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה heads off a challenge to the קל וחומר before anyone can raise it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might argue that getting the meat does not lead to getting the hide, since the מזבח gets the meat of an עולה but not its hide. The משנה answers that the מזבח is not a fair comparison, because it never receives hides at all. So the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Will prove (otherwise); a counter-example used to break a קל וחומר
In any case / anywhere

steps.whatToRemember: The כהנים get the hide of a valid עולה, including one slaughtered שלא לשמה and a woman's עולה. Hides of קדשי קדשים go to the כהנים by a קל וחומר; hides of קדשים קלים stay with the owners.

phrases.english: The altar cannot prove [otherwise],
phrases.notes: The objection would be: the מזבח gets the עולה's meat but not its hide, so meat doesn't bring hide.

phrases.english: since it does not get a hide in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the קל וחומר of step 5 against a possible counter-example
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the possible counter-example from the מזבח
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מזבח never receives hides, so it cannot show that getting the meat fails to bring the hide

steps.title: רבי יהודה: 'a man's burnt offering' excludes a consecrated-property offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא where רבי יהודה learns from 'עולת איש' that an עולה of הקדש is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'a man's burnt offering' comes to exclude a burnt offering of consecrated property. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that explains what the word 'איש' in the פסוק excludes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used 'עולת איש' to teach that the עולה must be valid. This ברייתא reads the word 'איש' as excluding something else: an עולה that belongs to הקדש and not to a private person. According to רבי יהודה, the כהנים would not get the hide of such an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא section (marks the start of the discussion)
To exclude / except for
Property consecrated to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: GEMARA:
The Rabbis taught: "a man's burnt offering"
comes to exclude a burnt offering of consecrated property.
phrases.notes: He means an עולה that belongs to the Temple treasury and not to a private person.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the פסוק quoted in step 1 and asks what 'איש' excludes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, 'עולת איש' excludes an עולה of הקדש.

steps.title: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה: it excludes converts' burnt offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה disagrees and says 'עולת איש' excludes the עולה of גרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי son of רבי יהודה says: it comes to exclude the burnt offering of converts.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא in the same ברייתא gives a different reading of the word 'איש'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that 'איש' excludes something, but they disagree about what. רבי יהודה says an עולה of הקדש. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says an עולה of גרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Converts

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
It comes to exclude the burnt offering of converts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה about what 'עולת איש' excludes
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, 'עולת איש' excludes an עולה of גרים.

steps.title: What does 'an עולה of הקדש' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of עולה רבי יהודה meant when he said 'עולת איש' excludes an עולה of הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'excluding an עולה of הקדש' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבי יהודה meant in step 7. This question sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every עולה is קדוש, so 'an עולה of הקדש' sounds unclear. The גמרא wants to know which specific case רבי יהודה had in mind, where the כהנים would not get the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; this leaves out a certain case
An עולה that belongs to הקדש (the Temple), not to a private person

phrases.english: What does 'to exclude an עולה of הקדש' mean?
phrases.notes: This goes back to רבי יהודה's teaching from 'עולת איש' in step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יהודה's view from step 7 to explain it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case is meant by 'an עולה of הקדש'?

steps.title: An עולה bought with leftover funds
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף explains that it means an עולה bought with leftover money from other offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said: it excludes an עולה that comes from leftovers.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר יוסף answers the question: רבי יהודה means an עולה bought with מותרות, leftover funds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leftover money from offerings is used to buy communal donated offerings. Such an עולה belongs to the public and not to one person, so it is not 'עולת איש', and the כהנים do not get its hide.

keyTerms.meaning: Leftovers; money or animals left over from offerings that were set aside
That comes from; bought with

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Yosef said:
To exclude an עולה that is brought from the leftovers.
phrases.notes: Leftovers means money left over from offerings set aside earlier, which is used to buy new offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף: פְּרָט לְעוֹלָה הֲבָאָה מִן הַמּוֹתָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עולה of הקדש is an עולה bought with leftover funds.

steps.title: But some say leftovers go to an individual's offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: this works if leftovers buy communal offerings, but not if they buy an individual's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who says leftovers go toward communal donated offerings. But for the one who says leftovers go toward an individual's donated offering, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי חייא בר יוסף's answer, because it only works according to one opinion about where leftover funds go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If leftovers buy a ציבור offering, the עולה is not 'עולת איש', so the exclusion makes sense. But if leftovers buy a יחיד offering, that עולה belongs to a person, so 'עולת איש' should include it and the כהנים should get the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well according to the one who says
A donated offering of the community
A donated offering of an individual
What can be said? (a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an argument against רבי יהודה himself. The גמרא is only asking whether רבי חייא בר יוסף's explanation of רבי יהודה works for every opinion.

phrases.english: This works well according to the one who says:
Leftovers go toward communal donated offerings;
But according to the one who says:
Leftovers go toward an individual's donated offering –
What can be said?
phrases.notes: In other words, that would be a man's עולה, so why shouldn't the כהנים get its hide?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חייא בר יוסף's explanation that 'עולת הקדש' means an עולה from leftovers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that leftovers buy an individual's offering, such an עולה is 'עולת איש', so it cannot be what the פסוק excludes.

steps.title: 'העולה' means a first עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רבא's teaching: 'העולה' means a 'first' עולה, so the hide goes to the כהן only from an animal first set aside as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבא said: 'העולה' means the first עולה. Here too, 'העולה' means a first עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the explanation from step 10. Even on the 'individual' view, a different word, 'העולה', excludes an עולה bought from leftovers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא learned from the extra 'ה' in 'העולה' that the תמיד must be the first offering of the day. The same word in the hide פסוק teaches that the כהן gets the hide only of a 'first' עולה, one set aside as an עולה from the start. An עולה bought from leftovers of another offering is not a 'first' עולה, so the כהן does not get its hide.

keyTerms.meaning: A first עולה; one that was an עולה from the beginning (or the first one of the day)
Here too

steps.whatToRemember: Even if a leftover-funded עולה belongs to an individual, the כהנים do not get its hide, because 'העולה' means only a 'first' עולה, one set aside as an עולה from the start.

phrases.english: As Rava said:
'The עולה' – the first עולה;
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:5. There it teaches that the daily תמיד must be the first offering of the day.

phrases.english: Here too, 'the עולה' – a first עולה.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:8, the פסוק about the hide of the עולה going to the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a separate textual source ('העולה') that excludes leftover offerings even on the individual view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An עולה bought from leftovers for an individual counts as 'עולת איש', so its hide would go to the כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'העולה' limits the hide to a 'first' עולה, so a leftover-funded עולה is excluded on either view.

steps.title: Another explanation: an עולה dedicated to בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: רבי אייבו, quoting רבי ינאי, explains differently: the phrase excludes someone who dedicates his עולה to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אייבו said in the name of רבי ינאי: it excludes someone who dedicates an עולה to the upkeep of the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer to the question of step 9: רבי יהודה's 'עולת הקדש' means an עולה whose owner also dedicated it to בדק הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the animal was set aside as an עולה, and then the owner also dedicated it to בדק הבית, the Temple upkeep fund. Since the owner tried to give it to הקדש, it is not treated as 'עולת איש', and the כהנים do not get its hide.

keyTerms.meaning: One who dedicates; puts something under a holiness it did not have before
The fund for upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Rabbi Aivu said in the name of Rabbi Yannai:
To exclude one who dedicates an עולה to the upkeep of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: פְּרָט לְמַתְפִּיס עוֹלָה לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different answer to the question of step 9, instead of רבי חייא בר יוסף's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An 'עולה of הקדש' is an עולה that its owner also dedicated to בדק הבית.

steps.title: Why רבי ינאי's teaching is a real new point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי ינאי's teaching holds even for those who say בדק הבית dedication normally does not take effect on altar-offerings, because it does take effect on the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is no need to say this according to the one who holds that dedicating something to בדק הבית takes effect by Torah law. The point is that even the one who holds it does not take effect agrees that this is only true for the meat. On the hide, the dedication does take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining the new point in רבי אייבו's teaching in the name of רבי ינאי. That teaching said that someone who dedicates his עולה to בדק הבית loses the כהנים' right to its hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בדק הבית dedication fully takes effect on altar-offerings, it is obvious that the כהנים lose the hide. The new point is that even the opinion that says it does not take effect agrees that it does take effect on the hide. Only the meat is held by the altar's holiness, so the hide is still open for the בדק הבית dedication to take hold of it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not necessary to say (the obvious case); the real new point is the harder case
Things dedicated for the upkeep of the בית המקדש
Take effect, take hold (as a dedication)
By Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of הקדש. One kind is offerings for the altar (קדשי מזבח). The other is property dedicated for upkeep of the בית המקדש (בדק הבית). The question is whether the second kind can take hold of something that already belongs to the first kind.

phrases.english: It is not necessary to say this according to the one who says:
dedication for Temple upkeep takes effect by Torah law;
phrases.notes: He means it takes effect even on an animal that was already set aside for the altar.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר לָא תָּפְסִי –
phrases.english: rather, even according to the one who says it does not take effect —
that applies only to the meat,
but on the hide it does take effect.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the new point in רבי ינאי's answer from step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even according to the view that בדק הבית dedication does not take effect on altar-offerings, it does take effect on the hide of an עולה, so the כהנים lose it.

steps.title: רב נחמן supports the leftover-money explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן, quoting רבה בר אבוה, says that 'עולת איש' leaves out an עולה bought with leftover money, the same as רבי חייא בר יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so said רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה: the words leave out an עולה that comes from leftover money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי חייא בר יוסף's explanation from step 10. It shows that another אמורא said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'וכן אמר' means 'and so said': a second voice agrees with the first explanation. This statement also sets up the next step, where רב המנונא attacks it.

keyTerms.meaning: And so said: another authority holds the same view
To leave out, to exclude
Leftover money from buying other offerings

phrases.english: And so said רב נחמן,
quoting רבה בר אבוה:
this leaves out an עולה that comes from leftover money.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי חייא בר יוסף's explanation (step 10) and shows that another אמורא agrees
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עולת איש' leaves out an עולה bought from מותרות, so the כהנים do not get its hide.

steps.title: רב המנונא: didn't רבי יהודה take this back?
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא challenges רב נחמן: his view follows רבי יהודה, and a ברייתא suggests רבי יהודה retracted it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said to רב נחמן: Whose view are you following? רבי יהודה's? But he took it back! As the ברייתא teaches: There were six boxes for gift offerings, used for עולות bought with leftover money, and the כהנים have no right to the hide. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא challenges רב נחמן's statement. It matches רבי יהודה, but רב המנונא says רבי יהודה changed his mind, and he begins to prove it from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first quotes רבי יהודה's original position: the כהנים do not get the hide of a leftover-money עולה. The proof that he took it back comes in the next steps, from what רבי נחמיה answered him.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom?
He took it back, he changed his mind
Six collection boxes for gift offerings in the בית המקדש
Have a right to, are entitled to

steps.confusionAlert: Up to 'דברי רבי יהודה', the ברייתא is only stating רבי יהודה's first opinion. It does not show the retraction yet; that comes from רבי נחמיה's answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הַמְנוּנָא לְרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: רב המנונא said to רב נחמן:
Whose view is this? רבי יהודה's?!
But he took it back!
As it is taught: six boxes for gift offerings —
for an עולה that comes from leftover money,
so that the כהנים have no right to its hide.
These are the words of רבי יהודה.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמַאן, כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה?! הָא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב נחמן's statement from step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's statement that 'עולת איש' leaves out a leftover-money עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That view depends on רבי יהודה, and רבי יהודה seems to have taken it back, so the view has no one to support it.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: you cancel יהוידע's teaching
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, רבי נחמיה (or רבי שמעון) objects to רבי יהודה: his view would cancel the teaching of יהוידע הכהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה said to him (some say it was רבי שמעון): If so, you have cancelled the teaching of יהוידע הכהן!
steps.whatsHappening: This is still inside the ברייתא. A תנא pushes back against רבי יהודה, and this objection is the evidence that רבי יהודה later took his view back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection says that רבי יהודה's rule goes against an older and well-known teaching. The next step quotes that teaching to show exactly where the conflict is.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
You have cancelled, made void
יהוידע the כהן גדול in the days of King יואש

phrases.english: רבי נחמיה said to him,
and some say it was רבי שמעון:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, בִּיטַּלְתָּ מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן!
phrases.english: If so, you have cancelled the teaching of יהוידע הכהן!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, בִּיטַּלְתָּ מִדְרָשׁוֹ שֶׁל יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from step 16 with an objection against רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's rule that the כהנים do not get the hide of a leftover-money עולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His rule goes against the older teaching of יהוידע הכהן.

steps.title: יהוידע's teaching: the hide goes to the כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The teaching of יהוידע הכהן says leftover money from a חטאת or an אשם buys עולות; the meat goes to the altar and the hide goes to the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned, יהוידע הכהן taught this: 'It is an אשם; he is surely guilty to ה''. Any money that comes because of a חטאת or an אשם should be used to buy עולות. The meat is for ה', and the hide is for the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes יהוידע's teaching to back up the objection against רבי יהודה. Its plain statement that the hide goes to the כהנים clashes with רבי יהודה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהוידע's teaching covers exactly the leftover-money case, and it gives the hide to the כהנים. The ברייתא shows no answer from רבי יהודה, and that silence is why רב המנונא says he took his view back. So רב נחמן's statement seems to be left without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching learned from a פסוק
'It is an אשם; he is surely guilty to ה'' (ויקרא 5:19)
Shall be bought with it
For ה' (burned on the altar)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה first said the כהנים do not get the hide of an עולה bought with leftover money. After he was challenged with יהוידע's teaching, which gives the hide to the כהנים, he seems to have taken his view back. That leaves רב נחמן's explanation of 'עולת איש' in question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This puts the leftover-money explanation of 'עולת איש' in doubt. רב נחמן therefore asks רב המנונא for his own reading, which comes in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, זֶה מִדְרָשׁ דָּרַשׁ יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן:
phrases.english: As it is taught: this is the teaching that יהוידע הכהן taught:
'It is an אשם; he is surely guilty to ה'' —

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁבָּא מִשּׁוּם חַטָּאת וּמִשּׁוּם אָשָׁם,
phrases.english: any money that comes because of a חטאת or because of an אשם,
עולות should be bought with it;
the meat is for ה', and its hide is for the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, זֶה מִדְרָשׁ דָּרַשׁ יְהוֹיָדָע הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source behind the objection in step 17
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's rule (no hide for the כהנים from a leftover-money עולה) cannot stand, so he took it back
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of יהוידע הכהן on ויקרא 5:19, which says the hide of such עולות goes to the כהנים

steps.title: Then how do you explain the words?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב המנונא how he explains 'עולת איש' if not the way רב נחמן did.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: So how do you, Master, explain it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן turns the question back on רב המנונא. If 'עולת איש' does not leave out an עולה bought with leftover money, what does it come to teach? This sets up רב המנונא's own explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא only knocked down רב נחמן's reading. But the words 'עולת איש' still have to teach something. So רב נחמן demands that רב המנונא give his own reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Master, a polite way of saying 'you'
How do you explain it? What case do you put it in?
'A man's עולה', words from the פסוק that רבי יהודה learns from

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: Here רב נחמן is speaking to רב המנונא.

phrases.english: But the Master, how does he explain it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב המנונא's challenge in steps 16-18 by asking for his alternative reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case does רב המנונא think 'עולת איש' leaves out?

steps.title: It is about someone who dedicates all his property
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא explains 'עולת איש' as dealing with someone who dedicated all his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I explain it as talking about a person who dedicates all his property.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא answers that the case is a person who dedicates everything he owns to the בית המקדש. His property includes animals that end up as עולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such an עולה is not just 'a man's עולה'. It came out of property that belongs to the בדק הבית fund. So the words leave this case out, and the כהנים do not get its hide.

keyTerms.meaning: One who dedicates all his property to the בית המקדש
I explain it as talking about

phrases.english: He said to him:
I explain it as one who dedicates his property.
phrases.notes: He means all his belongings, which go to the בדק הבית fund unless he says otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עולת איש' leaves out an עולה that comes from someone who dedicated all his property.

steps.title: The משנה about dedicated property: רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא says his reading fits רבי יהושע and brings the משנה. He starts with רבי אליעזר, who says all the animals are sold and the money goes to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: This follows רבי יהושע, as we learned: If someone dedicates his property, and among it are animals fit for the altar, male and female, רבי אליעזר says: The males are sold to people who need עולות. The females are sold to people who need שלמים. Their money joins the rest of the property for בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא brings a משנה that shows how a person's dedicated animals can become עולות. First comes רבי אליעזר's opinion, and רבי יהושע's comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that everything goes to בדק הבית. The animals are only sold so that someone else can offer them, and the money goes to the fund. In his view the donor's own animals are never offered for him. So רב המנונא needs רבי יהושע's view instead.

keyTerms.meaning: The fund for repairing and maintaining the בית המקדש
Fit to be offered on the altar
Shall be sold for the needs of, meaning to people who need them

phrases.english: And in line with רבי יהושע;
as we learned in a משנה:
One who dedicates his property
and among it there were animals
that are fit for the altar,
males and females –
רבי אליעזר says:
the males are sold for the needs of עולות,
the females are sold for the needs of שלמים offerings,
and their money goes in with the rest of the property
to בדק הבית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds רב המנונא's case from step 20 in a known משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That a person who dedicates his property can end up with his animals offered as עולות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שקלים, starting with רבי אליעזר's opinion.

steps.title: רבי יהושע's view: the males themselves are offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says the males are offered as עולות. The females are sold and their money buys עולות. Only the rest of the property goes to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: The males themselves are offered as עולות. The females are sold to people who need שלמים, and with their money he brings עולות. The rest of the property goes to בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of the משנה, the view that רב המנונא relies on. According to רבי יהושע, the person's own animals actually go up as עולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע understands that the donor wanted his altar-fit animals used for the altar. Only the rest of his property was meant for בדק הבית. This creates exactly the case of an עולה that came from 'dedicated property', which רב המנונא says 'עולת איש' leaves out.

keyTerms.meaning: They themselves are offered
And he brings with their money
The rest of the property

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר: sell the animals, and all the money goes to בדק הבית. רבי יהושע: the animals go to the altar as עולות, and only the rest goes to בדק הבית.

phrases.english: רבי יהושע says:
the males themselves are offered as עולות,
and the females are sold for the needs of שלמים
and with their money he brings עולות,
and the rest of the property goes to בדק הבית.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר זְכָרִים עַצְמָם יִקָּרְבוּ עוֹלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה begun in step 21 with the opinion רב המנונא relies on.
steps.raayaObject: That the dedicated animals themselves become עולות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע in the משנה in שקלים.

steps.title: Even רבי יהושע agrees the hide goes to בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says a person splits his dedication. Still, that only applies to the meat. The hide is taken by בדק הבית, so the כהנים do not get it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to רבי יהושע, who says a person splits his dedication, that is only for the meat. But the hide is taken by the dedication to בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא heads off a problem. If רבי יהושע gives the animals to the altar, maybe the hide should go to the כהנים like any עולה. He answers that the split only covers the meat, and בדק הבית keeps the hide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע holds that the donor divided his dedication: altar-fit things go to the altar, and the rest goes to בדק הבית. Only the meat is fit for the altar, so the hide stays in the בדק הבית portion. That is why 'עולת איש' tells us the כהנים do not receive this hide.

keyTerms.meaning: A person splits his dedication between different purposes
This applies only to
Takes hold, meaning the dedication grabs it

steps.whatToRemember: רב המנונא's reading: 'עולת איש' leaves out an עולה from someone who dedicated all his property. Even in רבי יהושע's view, the hide of that עולה belongs to בדק הבית and not to the כהנים.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע does not say the hide goes to the altar or to the כהנים. Only the meat goes to the altar. The hide is still held by the בדק הבית dedication.
steps.whyThisMatters: This links back to step 14: dedication to בדק הבית does take hold of the hide of an altar offering.

phrases.english: And even according to רבי יהושע
who says a person splits his dedication –
phrases.notes: He means: the animals go to the altar and the rest goes to בדק הבית, as in the משנה we just saw.

phrases.english: that applies only to the meat,
but the hide is taken hold of.
phrases.notes: The dedication to בדק הבית grabs the hide, so the כהנים don't get it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּאָמַר אָדָם חוֹלֵק הֶקְדֵּישׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies רבי יהושע's view from step 22 so that it fits רב המנונא's reading.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling (meat vs. hide)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהושע gives the animals to the altar, the hide should go to the כהנים like any עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The split dedication applies only to the meat. The hide remains held by בדק הבית, which is what 'עולת איש' teaches.

steps.title: Another view: 'a man's burnt offering' leaves out converts
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the words 'עולת איש' exclude the עולה of converts, so the כהנים do not get its hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: the words 'a man's burnt offering' come to leave out the burnt offering of converts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the second half of the ברייתא from step 8 and quotes it again so it can analyze it. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says 'עולת איש' excludes a convert's עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has finished explaining רבי יהודה's half of the ברייתא. It now turns to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's half, which reads 'איש' as leaving out a certain kind of owner, converts. This sounds strange right away, and that sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to leave out
The burnt offering brought by converts

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
[The words 'a man's burnt offering' come] to exclude the burnt offering of converts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion of רבי יהודה's view (steps 9-23) and returns to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's half of the ברייתא from step 8 in order to explain it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'עולת איש' excludes the עולה of converts from the rule that the כהנים get the hide.

steps.title: Isn't a convert also a man?
steps.stepSummary: רב סימאי בר חילקאי challenges רבינא: a convert is a man too, so how can 'איש' leave him out?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סימאי בר חילקאי said to רבינא: Is that to say a convert is not a man?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב סימאי בר חילקאי attacks רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's reading. A convert is a full Jewish man, so the word 'איש' should include him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is about the word itself. 'איש' fits a convert just as well as anyone else, so it cannot be the word that leaves converts out.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? (an opening for a surprised challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סִימַאי בַּר חִילְקַאי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Simai bar Chilkai said to Ravina:
Is that to say a convert is not a man?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's claim that 'עולת איש' excludes converts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A convert is an 'איש' like anyone else, so the word cannot leave him out.

steps.title: He means a convert who died with no heirs
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה is talking about a convert who died and left no heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: [It comes] to exclude a convert who died and has no heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge. He narrows the case: not every convert is excluded, only a convert who died without heirs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A convert usually has no Jewish relatives to inherit from him. If he died, his עולה no longer has a living 'איש' who owns it. So the word 'איש' leaves out this case, not converts in general.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert who died
Heirs

steps.confusionAlert: Don't take this to mean converts' עולות are less valid. Only the case of a convert who died with no heirs is excluded.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: פְּרָט לְגֵר שֶׁמֵּת וְאֵין לוֹ יוֹרְשִׁים.
phrases.english: [It comes] to exclude a convert who died and has no heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּרָט לְגֵר שֶׁמֵּת וְאֵין לוֹ יוֹרְשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה seemed to exclude every convert.
steps.terutzMaskana: He only excludes a convert who died with no heirs, whose offering has no owner.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's 'converts' means a convert who died without heirs: no living owner, so no hide for the כהנים.

steps.title: 'The hide of the burnt offering' includes converts, women and slaves
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says 'עולת איש' alone would only cover a man, but 'עור העולה' adds converts, women and slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'A man's burnt offering': I would only know about a man's burnt offering. From where do we know the burnt offering of converts, women and slaves? The verse says: 'the hide of the burnt offering', and that includes them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It teaches that the כהנים get the hide of an עולה brought by converts, women and slaves, too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עולת איש' alone sound limited to a man. The extra words 'עור העולה' broaden the rule to all owners. Now 'איש' is no longer needed to limit the owner, and the next step asks what it comes to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: I would only know...
From where do we know?
The hide of the burnt offering
It included (made the rule wider)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: ״עֹלַת אִישׁ״ – אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עוֹלַת אִישׁ;
phrases.english: 'A man's burnt offering': I would only know about a man's burnt offering;
from where do we know the burnt offering of converts, women and slaves?
The verse says: 'the hide of the burnt offering', so it included [them].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא on the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהנים get the hide of the עולה of converts, women and slaves, learned from 'עור העולה'.

steps.title: So what do the words 'a man's burnt offering' teach?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: if everyone is included, why does the פסוק say 'עולת איש'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if so, why does the verse say 'a man's burnt offering'?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks what job the words 'עולת איש' still have. This is a setup line, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since 'עור העולה' already includes all owners, 'איש' cannot be there to limit the owner. The words must teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: And if so
Why does the verse say...? (what does it come to teach?)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״עֹלַת אִישׁ״?
phrases.english: And if so, why does the verse say: 'a man's burnt offering'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 27: once everyone is included, 'איש' seems extra.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'עולת איש' come to teach.

steps.title: An עולה that counted for its owner, not one slaughtered for outside its time or place
steps.stepSummary: 'עולת איש' means an עולה that counted for the man. This leaves out one slaughtered with intent for outside its time or place, so the כהנים don't get its hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: A burnt offering that counted for a man. This leaves out one slaughtered [with intent] for outside its time or outside its place, so the כהנים have no right to its hide.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: 'עולת איש' means an עולה that worked for its owner. A disqualified עולה does not get its hide given to the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'איש' now describes the offering, not the owner: it must 'count' (עלתה) for a man. An עולה slaughtered with the wrong intent about time or place becomes invalid. So the כהנים lose the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: An עולה that counted for a man (did its job for the owner)
Outside its time
Outside its place
Have a right to; get

steps.whatToRemember: 'עור העולה' includes every kind of owner. 'עולת איש' teaches that only a valid עולה, one that counted for its owner, gives its hide to the כהנים.

phrases.english: A burnt offering that counted for a man;
phrases.notes: There's a play on words here: 'עולה' (burnt offering) and 'עלתה' (it counted).

phrases.aramaic: פְּרָט לְשֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטָה חוּץ לִזְמַנָּהּ וְחוּץ לִמְקוֹמָהּ,
phrases.english: to exclude one that was slaughtered [with intent] for outside its time or outside its place,
so that the priests have no right to its hide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'עולת איש' means an עולה valid for its owner. It excludes one slaughtered for outside its time or place from giving its hide to the כהנים.

steps.title: Maybe an עולה slaughtered for the wrong offering is also left out
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests: maybe an עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה should also lose its hide, since it did not count for the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that I include [in the exclusion] one that was slaughtered not for its own sake, since it did not count for the owner,
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible idea: an עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה also did not count for the owner, so maybe the כהנים lose its hide too. This is a setup, and the sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 29 linked the hide to the offering 'counting for the man'. An עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה does not count for the owner's obligation, so by that logic it should also be excluded. The 'יכול' shows this is only a first thought that the ברייתא will deal with next.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (opens an idea that will be tested)
Not for its own sake (slaughtered as a different offering)
Since
The owner of the offering

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ –
phrases.english: One might think that I include one that was slaughtered not for its own sake –
phrases.notes: He means include it in the exclusion, so the כהנים wouldn't get its hide either.

phrases.english: since it did not count for the owner,

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטָה שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the logic of step 29 to a new case.
steps.kashyaTarget: How far the rule of 'an עולה that counted for a man' reaches
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An עולה slaughtered שלא לשמה also does not count for the owner, so it seems the כהנים should lose its hide too.
